messages:
maya: Heads up — p99 spike right after runtime deploy v2.7.1 (commit ab12c9f). Seeing big tail regressions on prod routes.
sam: Confirmed. p95 up a bit but p99 exploded for a couple services. Noticed right around 10:02 UTC.
kevin: What changed in that release? Kernel selector tweak? microbatch defaults?
maya: Both, I think. Change summary in the deploy: `kernel_policy=aggressive_throughput`, `default_microbatch=16`.
pranay: That matches the rollout notes. We bumped microbatch to improve GPU utilization for high-throughput customers.
maya: Quick profiler snapshot from a hot endpoint: 
```
model: gpt-3x
commit: ab12c9f
kernel: fused_attention_v2
microbatch: 16
kv_cache_hit_rate: 67%
latency_percentiles_ms: p50=14 p95=110 p99=430
```
sam: Baseline before deploy was p99 ~120ms and kv_cache_hit ~98%. This is a big regression.
kevin: KV cache hit dropping that much explains tail. With more microbatching and fused kernel we might be forcing different token layouts / cache eviction patterns.
maya: Logs show a lot of `kv-cache-miss` and re-encoding work. Also saw GC-ish spikes on host during some batches.
pranay: Can we mitigate quickly by reverting one of the changes? Which is lower risk — kernel selector or microbatch?
kevin: Kernel selector seems like the largest immediate impact. The fused_attention_v2 gives throughput gains for long streams but has worse first-token recompute path and interacts badly with current KV layout. Reverting kernel_policy to `stable_latency` should help tail.
maya: Agree. Also lowering microbatch to 8 might bring latency down while we investigate.
maya: Proposed emergency plan: 1) rollback kernel_policy via config rollout to canary 2) monitor kv-hit + p99 3) if stable, roll to prod 4) open postmortem.
infra-bot: @maya initiated config rollback for runtime: kernel_policy -> stable_latency (canary). Rolling out to 5% canary now.
oncall: Canary telemetry: within 60s p99 trending back down, kv_cache_hit up to 94% on canary.
sam: Good signal. If canary holds for 5m we should flip full rollout.
infra-bot: Flip to 100% rollout initiated. Draining and restarting workers.
infra-bot: Rollback completed: runtime reverted to v2.7.0 kernel selector behavior.
maya: Post-rollback metrics: p50=13ms p95=92ms p99=135ms, kv_cache_hit_rate ~96-98% across routes.
kevin: Root cause hypothesis: kernel selector's `aggressive_throughput` policy preferred fused_attention_v2 which increases per-microbatch recompute on first token and changes memory access pattern — this increased KV cache churn when microbatch shapes changed. Combined with microbatch=16 we crossed a tipping point for tail.
pranay: Filing follow-ups: INF-789 (add perf/regression test for kernel selector under high kv-hit conditions), INF-790 (guard to blacklist aggressive kernels when kv_hit < 90%), INF-791 (add canary alert for kv_cache_hit < 92% or p99 > 200ms).
maya: Also suggests: add a smoke perf test in CI that runs a small KV-cache-heavy scenario and asserts p99 < 180ms.
kevin: Agreed. Also we should add telemetry to the selector so we can compute expected latency delta before picking a kernel (cheap estimator).
sam: FYI PR that introduced change: https://git.redwood/PR/4623 (revert already landed).
maya: Thanks everyone for the quick rollback. I'll draft a short incident note and attach traces/heatmaps. :white_check_mark:
pranay: I'll own INF-789 and start the regression tests today.
kevin: Follow-up owners assigned. We'll keep this as SEV3 for now until postmortem.
maya: Closing channel for now; reopen if anything else pops.
